title: Präsens und das V2-Gesetz
summary: Regular present-tense endings and German's non-negotiable rule: the finite verb always sits second

blocks.title: Präsens: die Endungen
blocks.body: Regular verbs follow one pattern. Take *machen* (to do/make): *ich mache, du machst, er/sie/es macht, wir machen, ihr macht, sie/Sie machen*. Six pronouns, six endings — learn the pattern once and it works for hundreds of verbs: *lernen, wohnen, kaufen, spielen, kochen*…

blocks.title: V2: das Verb ist immer an zweiter Stelle
blocks.body: German's most important word-order rule: in a main clause, the **finite verb is always the second element** — not necessarily the second word, the second **slot**. *Ich lerne heute Deutsch.* (I / lerne / today German.) Move *heute* to the front and the verb **stays** in slot two — the subject jumps after it: *Heute lerne ich Deutsch.* Never *Heute ich lerne Deutsch* — that's English word order, not German.
blocks.callout: Whatever you put first — subject, time, place — the verb holds position two like a law of physics.

blocks.title: Was auch vorne steht — das Verb bleibt zweite

pairs.note: Same meaning — *wohne* stays in slot two either way; only *ich* and *in Berlin* swap.
Front *heute* and the subject *ich* hops after the verb — V2 never breaks.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence has correct German word order?
blocks.explain: The verb *lerne* must stay in slot two; the subject *ich* moves after it. "Heute ich lerne" is English order, not German.

blocks.hint: The verb stays in slot two; the subject follows it.
blocks.explain: Heute arbeite ich viel. — *heute* takes slot one, *arbeite* holds slot two, *ich* comes right after.

blocks.title: Baue einen V2-Satz
blocks.prompt: Build a sentence that starts with a time word — the verb must stay in second place.

blocks.scene: Klaus tells you about his week in Cologne.

lines.speaker: Klaus
lines.target: Ich arbeite als Architekt hier in Köln.
lines.en: I work as an architect here in Cologne.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Und wie sieht dein Tag aus?
lines.en: And what does your day look like?

lines.speaker: Klaus
lines.target: Morgens arbeite ich, abends koche ich gern.
lines.en: In the mornings I work, in the evenings I like to cook.
lines.spotlight: *Morgens arbeite ich* — time word first, verb second, subject third. V2 in action.

lines.speaker: Klaus
lines.target: Ja, fast jeden Tag. In Köln kochen viele gern.
lines.en: Yes, almost every day. In Cologne, a lot of people like to cook.

questions.q: What does he do in the evenings?

blocks.prompt: Write 3 sentences about your day using regular present-tense verbs — start at least one with a time word (Heute, Morgens, Abends) and keep the verb in second place.
